inputs.userGoal: Set up a demo Fabric instance for this repo that is easy to spin up and spin down because it is expensive to keep running.
subGoals: Cost-optimized: use the smallest Fabric F SKU and suspend it whenever the demo is idle.
Usable demo: create a Fabric workspace, assign it to the capacity, and support GitHub integration.
Secret-safe: use interactive Entra authentication and never persist a GitHub PAT in the repository.

reasoning.whyChosen: Keeps every billable Azure resource for the demo in one disposable scope, supporting cost governance and a simple teardown path.
alternativesConsidered: Deploy into an existing shared resource group
reasoning.tradeoffs: Creating a dedicated resource group adds one management object but makes ownership, cost filtering, and deletion safer.

references.title: Manage Azure resource groups by using Bicep

resources.name: fcfabricgithubdemo

preflightChecks: F2 is available in the selected region
Each capacity administrator is a member of the Fabric tenant and is not a B2B guest

reasoning.whyChosen: F2 is the smallest pay-as-you-go Fabric capacity and supports pause and resume, directly meeting the cost-control requirement.
reasoning.tradeoffs: F2 has limited throughput and the workspace is unavailable while suspended, which is acceptable for an on-demand demo.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The Fabric capacity is deployed into the dedicated demo resource group.

references.title: Pause and resume your Fabric capacity

dataPlaneOperations.name: fabric-github-demo-workspace
dataPlaneOperations.operation: Create or reuse a workspace and assign it to the deployed capacity
dataPlaneOperations.lifecycle: The workspace persists while the capacity is suspended and is deleted only by the explicit destroy command.

dataPlaneOperations.name: github-workspace-connection
dataPlaneOperations.operation: Create a PAT-backed Fabric connection once, connect the workspace, and initialize synchronization
dataPlaneOperations.authentication: Prompt for the GitHub PAT without echoing or writing it to disk; subsequent operations use the Fabric connection ID
dataPlaneOperations.lifecycle: Optional one-time setup; teardown removes the Fabric workspace but never modifies or deletes the GitHub repository.

lifecycleCommands.deploy: Validate prerequisites, deploy the resource group and F2 capacity, create or reuse the Fabric workspace, then suspend the capacity.
lifecycleCommands.up: Resume the capacity and wait until it is active.
lifecycleCommands.down: Suspend the capacity and wait until it is paused.
lifecycleCommands.status: Show the Azure capacity state and configured Fabric workspace.
lifecycleCommands.connect: Prompt once for a GitHub PAT and connect the workspace to this repository.
lifecycleCommands.destroy: Require explicit confirmation, delete the Fabric workspace, and delete the dedicated resource group.

overallReasoning.summary: A single-region F2 capacity provides the least expensive paid Fabric environment. The Fabric workspace remains configured while the capacity is suspended, so normal use becomes a fast resume/suspend cycle rather than repeated provisioning.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: The design intentionally omits a virtual network, Key Vault, Log Analytics, an Automation account, and scheduled shutdown because the demo has no service-to-service secrets, exposes no application endpoint, and the user approved explicit lifecycle commands. GitHub integration still requires a one-time PAT because Fabric does not support automatic GitHub credentials for this API flow.

plan.validation: The subscription-scoped deployment creates the resource group before the resource-group-scoped capacity module. The workspace operation consumes the deployed capacity ID. Every declared dependency resolves, and destructive teardown requires confirmation.
